heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 prints Bambu PETG-CF exceptionally well up to a safe maximum print speed of 179 mm/s at 15 mm³/s flow, provided the stock stainless steel nozzle is upgraded. You must install a hardened steel hotend assembly before printing to prevent rapid abrasive wear from the embedded carbon fibers.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 15 mm³/s under Filament Settings > Basic Information to prevent underextrusion at high travel speeds.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm with a 0.2 mm Z-hop on retraction to minimize carbon fiber whisker stringing and nozzle buildup.
Set the First Layer Bed Temperature to 75°C and subsequent layers to 73°C to maintain bed adhesion without causing lower-layer heat softening.
Lower Part Cooling Fan thresholds to min 20% and max 50%, setting 'Keep fan always on' with layer time thresholds tuned for adequate inter-layer bonding.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking, inconsistent extrusion, or rapid nozzle wear
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Printing abrasive carbon-fiber-filled material through the stock stainless steel nozzle or insufficient melting temperature.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install the official Bambu Lab 0.4mm or 0.6mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly and increase printing temperature to 255°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing, fuzzy surface whiskers, and oozing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in hygroscopic PETG matrix compounded by carbon fibers facilitating capillary oozing.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated filament dryer at 65°C for at least 8 hours prior to printing and calibrate retraction to 0.8mm at 35 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Bed adhesion failure or PETG tearing PEI coating upon removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive adhesion between bare PEI and PETG copolymer, or bed temperature dropping below glass transition.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin layer of PVP glue stick or liquid glue to act as a separation release agent on the Textured PEI sheet, and raise the bed temperature to 75°C.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu PETG-CF with the stock Bambu Lab A1 hotend out of the box?
faq.answer: No. The stock A1 includes a stainless steel nozzle, which will rapidly erode from the abrasive carbon fibers. You must purchase and install the Bambu Hardened Steel Hotend before running PETG-CF.

faq.question: Does the Bambu Lab A1 require an enclosure to print PETG-CF?
faq.answer: No, an enclosure is not required. PETG-CF experiences significantly less thermal shrinkage and warping than ABS or Nylon, printing reliably on an open-frame bed slinger like the A1.

faq.question: Can I use the Bambu 4-in-1 AMS Lite with Bambu PETG-CF?
faq.answer: Yes, Bambu PETG-CF is fully compatible with the AMS Lite feeder system; however, frequent use will accelerate wear on the plastic PTFE guide funnels compared to standard PLA.

faq.question: Why is my PETG-CF print weak along the layer lines?
faq.answer: PETG-CF interlayer bonding suffers when printed with excessive cooling or too quickly. Limit maximum part cooling to 50%, ensure the hotend temperature is at 255°C, and keep volumetric flow within 15 mm³/s.
